91359.overview:
Uranians is a space themed shooter game for the BBC Microcomputer and Acorn Electron. It was developed by S Howitt and published by Bug-Byte.

Gameplay:

Uranians is a fixed shooter.

The Uranians, from the planet Uranus, are attacking! Destroy them, but be aware of the missiles they drop. A very big mothership flies at the top and sometimes drops a very big missile that will burst into flames upon impact.

91361.overview:
Uridium is a video game developed by Andrew Braybrook and ported to several home computers. It was converted for the BBC Microcomputer by AIM and published by Hewson.

Gameplay:

Your home solar system of 15 planets has been attacked by a horde of Super Dreadnoughts, from a race who wish to harvest your universe's minerals for their own use.

You must pilot your craft through some of the hardest levels ever created, shoot down enemy spacecraft and ground weapons, and avoid the many indestructible hazards. When a sufficient number of enemies have been defeated, the player can then land on the Dreadnought and proceed to destroy the ship's reactor.

The innovation is that you do not simply travel in a single direction, but instead move from left to right or right to left depending on where the current targets are, in a manner more similar to Defender than most shoot 'em ups.

122701.overview:
UIM is a 3D arcade adventure, an underwater version of Elite, set in a future where all life exists in the oceans.
You travel the oceans in a submarine, trading in commodities, shares and currency, and seeking the UIM.
You will need to purchase system and weapon upgrades to combat hostile forces.
There are over 65000 underwater ports with their own colonies to visit and over 250 missions to complete before you finally encounter the UIM.

125385.overview:
Ultron (working title Gorfon) was Written by Gary Partis for Audiogenic and was the sequel to his earlier game Positron.
Not to be confused with an Alligata game of the same name published by Viper.

The year is 2673 AD and the galaxy is under siege by aliens from the planet Gorfia. Your mission is to blast your way through wave upon wave of oncoming aliens, surviving long enough to take on and destroy the nerve centre of the alien attack - the Mothership. To do this, you have been given command of the most advanced space fighter in the Universe - the Ultron.

You begin your mission as a Cadet, but may rise through the ranks and become the ultimate Space Master. There are eight ranks to go through. Four screens go together to make up one wave. The screens are...
Space Swarmers: swarming mutants who release hordes of homing missiles.
Galactic Imps: approaching infantry whose sole aim is to infiltrate your defences.
Space Warp: aliens that loom out in 3D distracting you with the aim of disintegrating your craft.
Mothership: the aliens' supreme commander, situated in the nerve centre of the Mothership.

Occasionally, a reconnaissance ship will fly past, dropping missiles.

128046.overview:
This game was also released by Softspot as Electro Freddy.

You have to load products onto the conveyor - twelve are needed to move up a level. Avoid Uncle Claude who will throw objects at you or boot you out the door to the waiting ambulance. He's hired the evil corporation to protect his stock and so you must dodge the prickly acorns before they poison you. You can fight back and knock Claude down with one of his products, hitting him from above or below, and finally once all twelve are loaded he'll give up the key to the next level.
 
There are 11 Levels with each one featuring a different product (strip plug, cassette, watch, radio, camera, portable stereo, reel to reel tape recorder, synthesizer, TV set, cruise missile, BBC Model B).

206159.overview: Uggies Garden was written in 1990 but didn't see the light of day until 1997. The game was only released on the Play It Again Sam 19 compilation – it didn't get a standalone release. Play It Again Sam 19 wasn't released by Superior Software. A company called ProAction licensed the use of the name from Superior.

206172.overview:
Urban Upstart is a 2021 homebrew conversion of the 1983 ZX Spectrum / Commodore 64 text adventure of the same name. This version was developed by Darren Higgs and released into the public domain.

Game Description:

Urban Upstart is a text adventure with graphics set in a dead end town, somewhere in England, sometime in the 1980s.

Scarthorpe is a dead and dreary place, the kind of place that no-one ever visits and no-one can ever leave. It is a tough town, as the inlay says 'even the dogs carry flick knives'. The object of the game, therefore, is to find a way out of town.

The text parser allows the player to string commands together in the form 'TAKE BALL AND GO SOUTH'. The game can be saved when partially complete. The player's progress is measured by a scoring system, the maximum possible score being twenty two.

206632.overview:
Not to be confused with the Icon/Audiogenic game by Gary Partris with the same name.
This game was developed by Daniel Lucas and S A Subotsky for Alligata but they never released it themselves. Instead it was passed to Viper who published it.
Destroy all waves of aliens and avoid or destroy the asteroids, then dock with the mothership. All photon blasts missing their targets will be recorded as photon wastage and excessive wastage will result in the destruction of your laser base. After docking with the mothership, you will receive a bonus according to your shooting accuracy (measured by photon wastage).

420752.overview:
A U.S. Gold Master Series label compilation of 4 games originally released as individual titles by Ultimate Play The Game.

Jet-Pac: a gallery space shooter for up to 2 players by David Rhys Jones, originally released in 1983.

Knight Lore: a single player isometric arcade adventure by Paul Proctor, originally released in 1984. Third game in the Sabreman series.

Nightshade: a single player isometric arcade adventure by Paul Proctor. originally released in 1985.

Sabre Wulf: a single player arcade adventure by Paul Proctor, originally released in 1984. First game in the Sabreman series.

457119.overview: In this Bookware text adventure, based on one of the chapters of the Science Fiction short story series "The Unorthodox Engineers" by Colin Kapp. You take on the role of the protagonist Lieutenant Fritz van Noon and his band of "Unorthodox Engineers" as Dr. Maxwell Courtney asks you to try and discover the purpose of the indestructible pillar of darkness and its mysterious penumbral shadow, (hence the name "The Pen") which was (obviously?) left by an alien race on this otherwise normal planet. And you also have to solve the riddle of contra-energy. The objective of the story is outlined to the player during the opening stages of the adventure. The book with the short story that comes along with the game helps the player to better understand the story and contains some vital clues to solve some of the adventure's puzzles.
